alerts.title: Creatinine recorded only as pasted text
alerts.message: A creatinine result appears only in pasted lab text, so its date is unknown. Check when it was taken and enter it as a dated lab result for a patient on TDF.

alerts.title: NSAID use mentioned while on TDF
alerts.message: NSAID use is mentioned in notes for a patient on TDF. Consider reviewing renal risk and ensuring appropriate monitoring.

alerts.title: Proteinuria mentioned in notes
alerts.message: Proteinuria (or trace protein) is mentioned in notes. Consider follow-up assessment and management per local guidance.

alerts.title: Renal Function Decline
alerts.message: Guidelines state TDF can cause chronic kidney disease. Patient's creatinine levels have been rising from 0.9 mg/dL in 2020 to 1.4 mg/dL, indicating a decline in renal function. This could be due to TDF, but other non-drug causes such as dehydration or comorbidities should also be considered.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor renal function and consider alternative regimens if decline continues.

alerts.title: Fatigue and Potential Drug Attribution
alerts.message: Patient reports mild fatigue. Guidelines list exhaustion or extreme fatigue as potential side effects of TDF and DTG. However, the patient's busy work schedule could also be a contributing factor. Further evaluation is needed to determine the cause of fatigue.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess for non-drug causes of fatigue and consider monitoring or adjusting regimen if necessary.
